title: The youngest (1 Samuel 16)
hookLine: man sees the face, but the Lord beholdeth the heart; David is out with the sheep
carry: the lord looks at the heart

lines: A HORN OF OIL TO BETHLEHEM.
cards: Four hundred days in, and today is about being overlooked. Saul's reign has gone wrong, and God sends old Samuel to Bethlehem with a horn of oil, to the house of a man named Jesse, Isai in the Douay-Rheims.
One of Jesse's sons will be the next king. Jesse lines them up. The oldest, Eliab, walks in first, and he looks the part: tall, strong, the kind of man you'd cast as a king.
Samuel thinks, surely this is the one. After all, the last king was chosen standing head and shoulders above the crowd.

teach.b: And God stops him. In the Douay-Rheims: "Look not on his countenance, nor on the height of his stature." Then the line the whole chapter is built on: "man seeth those things that appear, but the Lord beholdeth the heart."
Notice the dig at height: yesterday the crowd cheered a king for being tall. So the parade goes on.

teach.h: SEVEN SONS, AND NONE IS CHOSEN.
teach.b: Seven sons pass in front of Samuel, and each time the answer is the same: the Lord hath not chosen this one. Samuel is puzzled. Are these all your sons?

teach.h: THE YOUNGEST, OUT WITH THE SHEEP.
teach.b: And Jesse says, almost as an afterthought: there's the youngest. He's out keeping the sheep. Nobody thought to call him in.
Samuel says: we won't sit down until he comes. They fetch him. And the text, honestly, says he was good-looking too, ruddy and handsome.
God's choice isn't against beauty; it just isn't based on it. The Lord says: arise, anoint him, for this is he.
Samuel pours the oil in the middle of his brothers, and the Spirit of the Lord comes upon David from that day on.
The pattern keeps coming back in the Bible: the younger brother, the overlooked one, the shepherd.
Catholics see it run all the way to Bethlehem again, where the son of David is born among shepherds, and to Mary's song: "He hath put down the mighty from their seat, and hath exalted the humble."

how: Catholics hear David's anointing at Mass, including on the Fourth Sunday of Lent in one year of the cycle, and Catholic preaching turns to it when speaking of how God chooses the humble and overlooked.

games.q: you're Samuel. seven of Jesse's sons have passed in front of you, and God has said no to every one. what do you do?
o: anoint the oldest anyway; he looks the part.
ask if there are any more sons.
go home and try another family.
games.why: he asks, are here all thy sons? there's the youngest, out with the sheep. Samuel won't sit down until he comes, and anoints him among his brothers.

practice: Walk in your mind through a room you'll be in soon, a family dinner, the pew at Sunday Mass, and find the one out in the field: the quiet one, the new one, the one who always does the dishes.
Wonder what they might be carrying, or what they're good at that nobody has asked about. If you pray, ask to see them the way the Lord sees, at the heart.

wordCard.voice: The youngest. David, Jesse's eighth son, left out in the fields with the sheep, and the one God chose because the Lord looks at the heart. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: heart, the inner self where a person thinks, chooses and loves. The Lord looks on the heart.

carryVoice: Your line: the lord looks at the heart. Height was never the measure. Four hundred days now, and i'm glad you're here.
